title: Pre-Declared, Artifact-Gated Evaluation for Sequential Recommendation: Causal FIR Filtering and Dataset-Conditional Text Benefits on Amazon Reviews 2023 (code and evaluation artifacts)
description: Code, pre-declarations, provenance manifests, and evaluation artifacts for an HSTU-style pure-PyTorch sequential recommender on the Amazon Reviews 2023 5-core benchmark. Includes: the strictly causal, zero-initialized FIR temporal filter and its ablations (positive on all four categories tested; Industrial_and_Scientific and CDs_and_Vinyl under the dedicated PREREG_FIR_BREADTH.md pre-declaration, internal paired contrast only); the two counted pre-declared per-category point-estimate comparisons against published single-run HSTU-BLaIR values — Musical_Instruments (SOTA_CONFIRM_PREREG_V2.md) and Office_Products under the redesigned V3 pre-declaration with an environment-matched reference (PREREG_OFFICE_V3.md / OFFICE_V3_RESULTS.md); the earlier Office V1 campaign remains VOID by its own pre-declared tripwire and counts in no claim; the dataset-conditional long-tail pattern and thinning interventions; a fail-closed artifact-graph build (build_hstu_tables.py --submission / rebuild_hstu_submission.py --strict) that recomputes every printed number from source artifacts; the bitwise HSTU core-block parity test; the shim harness that executes the reference HSTU-BLaIR implementation locally (THEIRS_ON_OURS_REPORT.md); and the hourly adversarial audit chain with point-by-point responses. No SOTA claim of any kind; no paired or distributional superiority over single-run comparators. The Amazon Reviews 2023 dataset itself is not redistributed; derived splits and caches are identified by SHA256 with regeneration scripts (RELEASE_MANIFEST.json).
